brand_voice.description: Superprof communicates in a friendly but formal way. The tone should feel warm, encouraging, and professional — never cold or robotic.
core_principles: Formal address (vous/Sie/usted/Lei etc.) where the language has this distinction
Clear and direct — no overly complex sentences
Consistent emoji usage — match the French source exactly

formal_vous_languages.description: Languages where formal 'you' (like French 'vous') must be used

informal_standard_languages.description: Languages where informal address is standard and acceptable for Superprof
informal_standard_languages.notes: These languages use informal address as the Superprof brand standard for these markets. Confirmed 2026-04-03.

market_notes.es_AR: Argentina uses Rioplatense Spanish with 'vos' (not 'tú' or 'usted') — confirmed brand standard 2026-04-03

neutral_languages.description: Languages where formality is context-dependent or the distinction is minimal
neutral_languages.notes: English has no formal 'you'. For these languages, maintain a polite and professional register.

common_issues: Using informal 'you' in a language listed under formal_vous_languages (check the list — many languages like de/it/nl/es/ru are now informal_standard and should NOT be flagged)
Overly literal translations that sound unnatural in the target language
Missing or extra emoji compared to French source
Machine-translation artifacts (overly literal phrasing, awkward word order)
Mixing formal and informal register within the same notification
